chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Ala' ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: When Noah (peace be upon him) descended from the ark, Satan came to him and said to him: 'There is no man on the earth greater than you in my favor; I supplicated to God against these corrupt people, and He relieved me of them. Shall I not teach you two characteristics? Beware of jealousy, for it is that which caused what happened to me; and beware of greed, for it is that which caused what happened to Adam.'
ai.seo_question: What two characteristics did Satan teach Noah to avoid?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Satan’s post-flood counsel to Prophet Noah, identifying envy (*al-hasad*) and greed (*al-hirs*) as the root causes of his own expulsion and Adam’s exile. This narrative underscores a key Shia theological perspective that these two traits are the primary architects of human spiritual decline, linking the primordial fall to the cosmic rebellion of Iblis.
